entries.text: You have power over your mind — not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.
The happiness of your life depends upon the quality of your thoughts.
Confine yourself to the present.
Waste no more time arguing what a good man should be. Be one.
Very little is needed to make a happy life; it is all within yourself, in your way of thinking.
The best revenge is not to be like your enemy.

Begin the morning by saying to thyself, I shall meet with the busybody, the ungrateful, arrogant, deceitful, envious, unsocial. All these things happen to them by reason of their ignorance of what is good and evil.
Look within. Within is the fountain of good, and it will ever bubble up, if thou wilt ever dig.
Accept the things to which fate binds you, and love the people with whom fate brings you together, and do so with all your heart.
Nothing happens to any man which he is not formed by nature to bear.
It is not death that a man should fear, but he should fear never beginning to live.
A man's worth is no greater than the worth of his ambitions.
When you arise in the morning, think of what a precious privilege it is to be alive — to breathe, to think, to enjoy, to love.
Everything we hear is an opinion, not a fact. Everything we see is a perspective, not the truth.
Dwell on the beauty of life. Watch the stars, and see yourself running with them.
The object of life is not to be on the side of the majority, but to escape finding oneself in the ranks of the insane.
Loss is nothing else but change, and change is nature's delight.
If it is not right, do not do it; if it is not true, do not say it.
The soul becomes dyed with the color of its thoughts.
How much time he saves who does not look to see what his neighbor says or does or thinks.
The universe is change; our life is what our thoughts make it.
Receive without pride, let go without attachment.
Do every act of your life as if it were your last.
That which is not good for the bee-hive cannot be good for the bees.
If thou art pained by any external thing, it is not this thing that disturbs thee, but thy own judgment about it; and it is in thy power to wipe out this judgment now.
Never esteem anything as of advantage to you that will make you break your word or lose your self-respect.
Remember that very little is needed to make a happy life.
The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.
Be like the promontory against which the waves continually break; but it stands firm and tames the fury of the water around it.
The best answer to anger is silence.
It never ceases to amaze me: we all love ourselves more than other people, but care more about their opinion than our own.
Let not the future disturb thee, for thou wilt arrive there, if thou shalt arrive, with the same reason which now thou usest for the present.
Accept whatever comes to you woven in the pattern of your destiny.
The art of living is more like wrestling than dancing.
If it is not right, do not do it. If it is not true, do not say it. For the greatest mind must be, above all, master of itself.
No man is happy who does not think himself so.
Think not disdainfully of death, but look on it with favor; for even this is one of those things which nature wills.
Each thing is of like form from everlasting and comes round again in its cycle.
What we cannot bear removes us from life; what remains can be borne.
Thou canst live well. Then thou canst die well also.
All is ephemeral — fame and the famous as well.
Adapt thyself to the things with which thy lot has been cast; and the men among whom thou hast received thy portion, love them, and do it truly, sincerely.
Do not act as if thou wert going to live ten thousand years. Death hangs over thee. While thou livest, while it is in thy power, be good.
He who lives in harmony with himself lives in harmony with the universe.
Be tolerant with others and strict with yourself.
Whatever happens to you has been waiting to happen since the beginning of time.
Do not be ashamed to be helped.
Nowhere can man find a quieter or more untroubled retreat than in his own soul.
entries.long: Marcus writes that people retreat to the country, the seashore, the mountains — but the shortest journey to peace is inward. The retreat of the soul is always open, free of charge, and near at hand.

entries.text: External things are not the problem. It is your assessment of them. Which you can erase right now.
Our life is what our thoughts make it.
Whenever you are about to find fault with someone, ask yourself the following question: What fault of mine most nearly resembles the one I am about to criticize?
The present is all that they can give up, since that is all you have, and what you do not have, you cannot lose.
All things are interwoven with one another; a sacred bond unites them.
What is not good for the swarm is not good for the bee.
Think of yourself as dead. You have lived your life. Now, take what is left and live it properly.
